title: Field pilot privacy operational plan + DPA redlines
content:
Summary:

This is a working operational plan and DPA addendum redline for an upcoming field pilot (customer: Acme Financial) that will exercise streaming text generation from Redwood Hosted API and a dedicated private deployment for regulated PII workloads. The goal is to document a pragmatic data handling and retention regime for the 3-month pilot, propose minimal DPA addendum language the legal team can adopt, and capture open technical/workshop items for solutions engineering and SRE.

High-level objectives:
- Ensure pilot meets Acme’s data sovereignty and retention constraints while allowing useful debugging telemetry.
- Minimize storage of sensitive inputs by default; provide reversible steps for debugging only when explicitly authorized.
- Produce a DPA addendum draft that legal + security can iterate on quickly.
- Define operational runbooks for automated deletion, redaction, and auditability for pilot scope.

Scope (what this doc covers):
- Ingest paths: Hosted API ingestion, Dedicated (VPC) ingestion, and ad-hoc uploads via SFTP for training prompts.
- Data types in scope: customer-supplied prompts, system prompts, model outputs, inference logs (latency/trace), request metadata (IP, region, headers) and debug traces containing KV cache snapshots.
- Retention windows and deletion mechanics for each artifact type during pilot.
- Proposed redline language for DPA addendum covering limited retention, access controls, and breach notification timelines.
- Workshop notes / unresolved decisions and next steps.

Architectural assumptions for pilot:
- Two deployment modes: Redwood Hosted (sandbox account) for non-PII development flows, and Redwood Private (VPC) for regulated PII paths.
- All PII traffic to be tagged at request level by customer via request header X-Acme-PII: true/false. Solutions engineer will provide sample middleware to automatically set this based on pattern matches.
- Telemetry collection separated by ingestion mode: Hosted telemetry goes to a sandbox analytics project with 30d retention; Private telemetry is stored in customer-owned S3 (or equivalent) with lifecycle managed via pilot config.

Recommended data handling and retention policy (pilot-level):
1) Customer prompts (raw text):
   - PII=false: retain for 7 days for debugging, then auto-delete.
   - PII=true: default do NOT persist. If persistence is required for debugging, require an explicit ticket (JIRA-SE-1427) and allow retention up to 30 days with customer-signed justification.
   - Storage mechanism: ephemeral in-memory KV cache until response generation completes. Persistent writes only to auditable, access-restricted buckets.
2) Model outputs (generated text):
   - Retain 7 days for non-PII flows; otherwise default DELETE unless customer opts in.
3) Inference logs (latency, model selection, token counts):
   - Keep aggregated telemetry indefinitely (no raw text). Aggregates stored in internal metrics DB with role-based access.
4) Full request/response traces (debug traces with tokens or KV snapshots):
   - Never persisted by default. Persist only under scoped debugging mode (approved ticket + timeboxed window). Any persisted trace must be encrypted with CMK and stored in customer-designated bucket for the pilot.
5) Audit logs (who accessed persisted artifacts):
   - Retain 365 days; exportable as csv for audit requests.

Deletion and redaction workflows:
- Automated retention enforcement task runs daily and enforces TTLs. Files marked for deletion are moved to a pending-delete folder for 48 hours, then permanently deleted.
- Emergency purge API: available to customer and Redwood SOC; executes immediate scrub and returns proof-of-deletion digest. Proof-of-deletion will include file id, deletion timestamp, and storage checksum before deletion.
- Redaction helper: provide best-effort redaction SDK that can remove detected PII tokens from stored artifacts; redaction events are recorded in audit logs.

Access controls and segregation of duties:
- Minimum-privilege access model: solutions engineers, SREs, and customer admins have scoped roles. Support staff require explicit ticket (and timeboxed elevated access) plus a two-person approval.
- Access to any persisted PII artifacts requires MFA and justification stored in Jira ticket.

Proposed DPA addendum redlines (initial language suggestions):
- "Purpose limitation": Redwood will process customer data solely for the purposes of providing the Services under the Pilot Agreement and solely in accordance with the retention schedule outlined in Appendix A (Pilot Retention Schedule).
- "Default non-persistence": Except where Customer expressly enables persistence for a given data flow through documented configuration, Redwood will not persist full request or response text labelled PII and will only retain metadata and aggregates as described in Appendix A.
- "Debugging exceptions": Persistence of PII for debugging requires explicit Customer written authorization per-ticket; Redwood will log the authorization, the ticket id, the exact artifacts persisted, and the retention TTL.
- "Breach notification": Redwood will notify Customer within 48 hours of confirmed unauthorized access to persisted Pilot PII artifacts and will provide remediation steps consistent with the Master Services Agreement.
- "Proof of deletion": Upon Customer request, Redwood will provide cryptographic proof-of-deletion for artifacts subject to deletion under the Pilot Retention Schedule within 5 business days.

Operational runbooks (short-form):
- Onboarding checklist for pilot:
   1) Confirm data flows and PII tagging rules with Acme data owner.
   2) Create pilot-specific storage projects/buckets with lifecycle rules.
   3) Deploy request-level PII gating middleware and validate via canned test suite.
   4) Configure automated retention tasks and emergency purge API access.
- Debugging flow:
   1) Customer or SE raises Jira ticket and documents required artifacts and retention justification.
   2) SE requests two-person approval from SE lead + security to enable persistence flag.
   3) SE collects artifacts and tags them with ticket id and TTL.
   4) After TTL, automated deletion runs and proof-of-deletion posted to ticket.

Workshop notes and unresolved questions (captured during 2025-01-28 customer workshop):
- Acme asks for 90-day default retention for outputs for business continuity; we recommended 30 days for pilot, escalate if necessary.
- Need legal sign-off on "proof-of-deletion" format - whether checksums are sufficient.
- Clarify whether customer requires egress logging (full request header capture), which may reveal IP addresses tied to personal data.
- Confirm whether Acme prefers customer-owned encryption keys for private deployment (recommended for compliance).
- SRE request: provide sample scripts for emergency purge that can be executed by on-call with RBAC gating.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: accidental persistence of PII in hosted sandbox. Mitigation: default sandbox config enforces no-persist flag and daily audits.
- Risk: delayed deletion due to backup retention. Mitigation: include backup retention policy in Pilot Retention Schedule and ensure backups are also lifecycle-managed with same TTLs.

Next steps and owners:
- Legal (Priya Nair): iterate DPA addendum redlines and return by 2025-02-07.
- Solutions Eng (Maya Patel, Diego Alvarez): deliver middleware and test harness for PII tagging by 2025-02-05.
- SRE (Connor Lee): publish emergency purge runbook and sample scripts by 2025-02-03.
- Customer (Acme data owner): confirm retention targets and key management preference by 2025-02-10.

Appendix A: Pilot Retention Schedule (summary table):
- Raw prompts (PII=true): default DO NOT PERSIST; exception retention up to 30 days with ticket.
- Raw prompts (PII=false): 7 days.
- Model outputs: 7 days (default) or 30 days if customer opts in for specific flows.
- Aggregated telemetry: indefinite (no PII).
- Audit logs: 365 days.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally conservative for the pilot to reduce legal friction. If customer pushes back, we can widen retention windows but must document business justification in the ticket.
- Please ensure all redline language is copied into Confluence page CONF-Privacy-Field-Pilot-Plan for version tracking.

Document history and edits:
- 2025-01-15: initial draft (Maya).
- 2025-01-28: customer workshop notes added (Maya, Diego).
- 2025-01-30: SRE runbook stub added (Connor).
- 2025-02-03: updated DPA language suggestions after legal sync (Priya).

End of document.
